beats.t: They descended along the root for a long time. Where darkness ended stood one tree, larger than all five skies combined.
Small papers hung from its branches instead of leaves. Each bore eight spaces: someone's birth year, month, day, and hour.
The World Tree. The tree holding every Four Pillars chart. A legend among fortune-tellers. It really exists.
Every paper is a person?
Yes. Yours, mine, Yeoni's mother's—somewhere up there.
(Mom's too. Somewhere there.)
Don't look for it. Once you see it, you'll want to touch it. These papers hold other people's time.
I won't. It's enough to know it's there.
Yeoni looked up. Paper leaves rustled whenever the wind blew. Billions of birthdays whispering at once.
But another sound mingled with the rustling. Something gnawing.
A black hole had opened in the middle of the trunk. Seed-sized Black Moon was burrowing inside. Growth rings around the hole blackened one by one.
It's eating the rings. Each line is a year of someone's life.
Several paper leaves fluttered from above. Their writing vanished before they reached the ground.
What happens to those people when their papers are erased?
In reality, someone loses a year. A birthday slips from memory, or a name grows faint. Like what happened to me.
The roots are drying. I'll water them.
Seo Hanbi held the umbrella upside down. Rain gathered in it, then overflowed, soaking along the roots. Withered rootlets lifted one by one.
I should do something too. Burn that thing out?
No! This is a tree! Set it on fire and the world becomes firewood!
Fire's the only thing I know!
Warmth, not fire. You did it on our island. When the sun rose.
Moka closed his mouth, then pressed both paws to the trunk. Warmth spread instead of flame. Frost melted from the bark. Sleeping birds among the leaves woke.
So that's how. Warming without burning.
Moka, that was rather impressive.
Don't praise me. It's awkward. You were easier when you wrote ledgers.
Seo Hanbi laughed aloud. Droplets at the umbrella's tip trembled with her laughter.
I'll widen the hole and pull it out.
Neo raised a hand. A golden blade formed at his fingertips, then stopped just before touching the tree.
Why stop?
My power cuts Wood. To get it out, I'd have to split this trunk too.
Neo's hand trembled. Yeoni remembered matching breaths with him on the island. His voice saying he could hurt them.
Then don't cut. Support it. Like you supported me.
Neo withdrew the blade and braced the trunk with both hands. Gold wrapped the tree like a prop. The splitting growth rings stopped.
This won't get it out. But I can keep the tree from falling.
That's right. That's always been your part. Supporting.
Support it. Hold on. In the end, I am still inside.
A black hand reached from the trunk. Not hundreds this time. Just one, thick and enormous. It crawled upward along the grain.
This tree is my final body. To remove me, you must kill it. To save it, you must leave me.
Coward! Hiding in someone else's home and threatening us!
That is how I live. Entering empty places. Your vessel has filled, so this is all I have left.
Yeoni turned those words over. Living in empty places. A place that admits anything because it is empty.
(Empty. An empty place. Where did I hear that?)
Yeoni turned. Yundal was already removing his glove.
You know it too. Emptiness is hungry. I was only hungry from the beginning.
I know you're hungry. But you can't eat other people's birthdays. Those belong to them.
Then what should I eat? I have no birthday.
Yeoni couldn't answer. The question lingered strangely in their ears. Something without a birthday. Something no one called by name.
Yeoni. I thought what you just thought too.
No. I didn't think it. I really didn't.
Emptiness eats emptiness. My palm is the hole Black Moon first made. It opened when Blue Rabbit ate my hour. It belonged to that thing originally.
So I'm giving it back. To its owner. Very tightly.
If you swallow it, you'll...
I know. We don't know how large the Void will grow. I might be emptied with it.
That isn't repayment. It's simply disappearing.
I'll do it. I used to be on Black Moon's side. The one who owes a debt should do it.
Your hands are Water, Seo Hanbi. Water can't fill a hole like this. It just flows in. This has to be my hand.
Never thought I'd hear that from you. You've grown, our ledger expert.
Smiling, Yundal pressed his bare palm against the black hole in the trunk. The dark circle spreading to his wrist met it.
A sucking sound rose, like a very long, deep breath. The black hand tore free of the trunk and was drawn into Yundal's palm.
Let go. This is my hole. I made it.
Exactly. You made it. You should fill it.
Yundal's face went white. The black circle spread beyond his wrist to his elbow. His outline began fading.
Uh, that person. Who was he? His name...
Moka stopped mid-sentence. His lips moved, but no name came out. He looked shocked at himself.
Yundal!
Yeoni shouted. The name hung in the air. At its sound, Yundal's outline sharpened a little.
That's an alias. A month that exists and doesn't. It doesn't stick well.
Alias or not, it's the name we called you! Neo came back with a nickname!
Yundal. Yundal.
Yundal! You can ask my birthday! I'll tell you everything!
Each time his name was called, another layer of Yundal's outline returned. Four voices held him to the ground.
Yundal. I'm not done telling you to take your hand off Yeoni's shoulder. Come back.
Ah, that makes me want to return. To be envied.
The last strand was swallowed. The black circle on Yundal's palm contracted. Smaller, smaller. Finally, one dot.
Then even the dot vanished. What remained was an ordinary palm. Lines, calluses, a slight tremble.
Black Moon's voice was gone. The last thing left was a tiny sigh. No one could tell whether it was a sigh of fullness or hunger.
(Goodbye. Next time, be born somewhere you have a birthday.)
It closed. The Void. Emptiness ate emptiness, and filled.
Yundal clenched and opened his hand again and again, as though the feeling of closing it were new.
The trunk's hole healed too. Blackened growth rings returned to brown. Fallen paper leaves rode the wind back to their branches.
Yundal. I remember your name. Why couldn't I before? Sorry.
It's fine. I don't know my own name either.
At that moment, a small light rose above Yundal's wrist. A clock hand. Five twenty. It stopped precisely there.
[ Hour of the Rabbit · 05:20 · Returned ]
My hour. My real hour. Five twenty in the morning. Just before sunrise.
Yundal said nothing for a long time. Then he rubbed his eyes with the back of his hand. No one teased him.
Your name too? Your real name?
Secret. We're not home yet. I'll tell you at my front door.
Smooth to the very end.
You too, Mr. Cat. Your voice trembled when you called my name.
It did not.
It did. I heard. One more star.
The treetop opened. From the tip of its highest branch, a card descended slowly. A blank card with no illustration.
Only a number appeared at the top: 23. The name field was empty. No picture, no words.
The twenty-third card. A destiny no one has written yet.
If it's empty, won't someone come to eat it again?
That's why someone must write it. This time a writer, not a devourer.
Then Yeoni's phone rang in their pocket. It hadn't rung once since they entered this world.
[ Customer Support: Universe · 1 waiting to connect ]
One waiting. Not 9,999.
Answer. This time, they'll pick up.
Yeoni paused their thumb over the call button. Everyone watched: Moka, Yundal, Seo Hanbi, Neo. Not one missing.
Ready to write my review. A five-star one.
